# Results — Study 690 (Three Stars in the South) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
rare bullish **three stars in the south** (three consecutive black candles, each with a
**shrinking** intrabar range and a **rising low**, in a downtrend) marks the exhaustion
of the sell-off — encoded as two honest cuts: a **loose** cut (three shrinking bearish
candles with strictly rising lows, sitting in a genuine downtrend) and a **strict**,
literature-closer cut (the loose cut, plus a hammer-like first star, a no-gap second
star, and a near-marubozu third star that never breaks the second star's low). Both are
pinned against the **downtrend-matched base rate** — the same long bet on every bar that
already sits in a matching downtrend. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar
month; the partial current month is dropped). Panel fingerprint `16a85c8367ed`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, **61 names** (SPY + 60 long-listed US large-caps spanning every major sector), cache-first |
| Window | ~25.0 years per name, ~2001 → 2026-06-30, **383,080** total daily bars |
| Sample fingerprint | SPY: `27b74051eb44` (6,280 rows, 2001-07-10 → 2026-06-30) |
| Detector | loose = 3 bearish candles with strictly shrinking intrabar range and strictly rising lows, after a downtrend context (close 2 bars back below its level 10 sessions earlier); strict = loose + a real lower shadow on the first star (hammer-like), the second star opening inside the first star's real body (no gap down), and a near-marubozu third star (small shadows both sides) that never breaks the second star's low |
| Execution / costs | pattern confirmed on the close of the 3rd star; entered at the **next open** (one documented lag); long-only; **5 bps** one-way × 2 (round trip); no borrow |
| Statistics | Welch *t* of star reversal mean vs the downtrend-matched base-rate mean (the decisive test); one-sample HAC *t* where n permits; a 2,000-draw label-shuffle placebo; **Bonferroni** correction across 4 horizons (critical \|*t*\| ≥ **2.50**); below **8** pooled events, no *t*-stat is computed at all |

No survivorship on the Signal axis in the sense that matters here: this is a
single-pattern event study (not a cross-sectional portfolio), so a fixed,
currently-liquid basket affects which *names* contribute events, not the direction of
the star-vs-base-rate comparison.

## The detector — how rare is a real "shrinking, rising-low" three-star, really?

| cut | definition | count (pooled, 61 names, 25y) | rate |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| **Loose** | 3 shrinking bearish candles + rising lows + downtrend context | **363** | ~0.24 / ticker-year (≈ once per 4.2 ticker-years) |
| **Strict** (literature-closer) | + hammer 1st star, no-gap 2nd star, marubozu 3rd star | **5** | ~0.003 / ticker-year (≈ once per **305** ticker-years) |

The strict cut is not just rare, it is the rarest pattern this desk has measured: demanding
the actual hammer-first / no-gap-second / marubozu-third geometry Nison describes collapses
the candidate pool by more than 70× versus the loose cut, and leaves only **5** occurrences
across 1,525 ticker-years of data — squarely matching Bulkowski's own published caution that
he could not find enough real occurrences to rank the pattern with confidence.

## Loose cut — three shrinking, rising-low black candles in a downtrend (n = 363)

Bonferroni-corrected critical \|*t*\| for 4 simultaneous horizons: **2.50**.

| horizon | n | star mean | win% | base rate | delta (star − base) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d  | 363 | +21.9 bps | 55.1% | +2.4 bps | **+19.5 bps** | **+2.26** | 0.015 | +11.9 bps |
| 5d  | 363 | +43.3 bps | 54.8% | +28.8 bps | **+14.5 bps** | **+0.74** | 0.263 | +33.3 bps |
| 10d | 363 | +69.2 bps | 57.6% | +57.2 bps | **+12.0 bps** | **+0.45** | 0.349 | +59.2 bps |
| 20d | 363 | +90.3 bps | 55.9% | +119.4 bps | **−29.1 bps** | **−0.80** | 0.768 | +80.3 bps |

**No horizon clears the Bonferroni bar.** The 1-day reaction is the closest thing to a
signal here (nominal *t* = 2.26, placebo *p* = 0.015) but falls short of the corrected
2.50, and it does not hold up: by 20 days the sign has **flipped** — the star events
trail the base rate by 29 bps, not lead it. A pattern with a genuine, persistent
exhaustion edge should not reverse sign as the holding period lengthens.

## Strict cut — the literature-closer three stars in the south (n = 5)

| horizon | n | star mean | win% | delta (star − base) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d  | 5 | +37.6 bps | 60.0% | **+35.2 bps** | too few to test | 0.302 | +27.6 bps |
| 5d  | 5 | −57.9 bps | 40.0% | **−86.7 bps** | too few to test | 0.719 | −67.9 bps |
| 10d | 5 | +27.8 bps | 60.0% | **−29.4 bps** | too few to test | 0.555 | +17.8 bps |
| 20d | 5 | +133.0 bps | 40.0% | **+13.6 bps** | too few to test | 0.486 | +123.0 bps |

With only **5** pooled events (below `MIN_N_FOR_TEST` = 8), no *t*-statistic is computed
at any horizon — a *t* on 5 points would be theatre, not evidence. The raw numbers are
reported for transparency only: the delta sign **flips at every horizon**
(+35, −87, −29, +14 bps), which is exactly what pure noise on a 5-point sample looks
like, not a persistent effect struggling to reach significance.

### The strict cut's five events, in full (there are only five)

| ticker | star block | 20-day return (bps) | context |
|---|---|--:|---|
| TXN | 2006-10-18 → 2006-10-20 | **−303.3 bps** (−3.03%) | a mid-decline star, no reversal followed |
| CAT | 2021-06-14 → 2021-06-16 | **−256.3 bps** (−2.56%) | a mid-decline star, no reversal followed |
| BDX | 2016-09-16 → 2016-09-20 | **−210.2 bps** (−2.10%) | a mid-decline star, no reversal followed |
| AXP | 2019-03-27 → 2019-03-29 | **+624.1 bps** (+6.24%) | a genuine sharp bounce followed |
| COST | 2024-10-24 → 2024-10-28 | **+810.9 bps** (+8.11%) | a genuine sharp bounce followed |

Two of five events land on real, sizeable bounces (AXP, COST); three do not (TXN, CAT,
BDX kept falling). With n = 5 this is a coin flip's worth of evidence in either
direction — naming all five, rather than cherry-picking the winners, is the point.

## Costs — net of a 5 bps one-way round trip (10 bps total)

| horizon | loose gross | loose net | strict gross | strict net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1d  | +21.9 bps | +11.9 bps | +37.6 bps | +27.6 bps |
| 5d  | +43.3 bps | +33.3 bps | −57.9 bps | −67.9 bps |
| 10d | +69.2 bps | +59.2 bps | +27.8 bps | +17.8 bps |
| 20d | +90.3 bps | +80.3 bps | +133.0 bps | +123.0 bps |

Costs are not the binding constraint anywhere in this table — most cells stay positive
net of a 10 bps round trip. What kills this pattern is that the point estimate is not
statistically certified at any horizon (loose) and that the strict, literature-faithful
cut fires so rarely (~once per 305 ticker-years) that there is no meaningful capacity to
deploy it even on the horizons where the raw number happens to look good.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic panel: 60 names, ~13.9 years each, forced 3-bar shrinking/rising-low blocks
planted **only where the underlying random walk is already in a downtrend on its own** (no
artificial drift is injected elsewhere on the tape, so star events and the base rate are
drawn from the same population) at a controlled rate, with a TUNABLE planted post-pattern
bounce (knob `edge`); no network. The decisive statistic is the same Welch *t* of star mean
vs base-rate mean used on the real tape.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.34** (sd 1.08), \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.02 (seed 690) | delta **+156.0 bps**, Welch *t* = **+7.44** |
| planted edge = 0.04 (seed 690) | delta **+346.9 bps**, Welch *t* = **+16.16** |

The null is well-calibrated (mean close to zero, firing at roughly the textbook rate —
in the same ballpark as sibling 685's tri-star-doji null), and a modest planted bounce
lights up cleanly and monotonically at *t* = 7.44 and 16.16. Per the desk's standing
rule, **a synthetic control never backs a Signal stamp** — it exists only to prove the
harness can find a real, planted effect, which it demonstrably can. The honest,
unglamorous real-tape result above stands on its own.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The loose cut (n = 363) comes closest at 1 day (Welch *t* = 2.26,
  placebo *p* = 0.015) but falls short of the Bonferroni-corrected bar (\|*t*\| ≥ 2.50,
  4 horizons) — and its own sign **reverses** by 20 days (delta −29.1 bps). The
  literature-closer strict cut fires only **5** times in 25 years across 61 names
  (below `MIN_N_FOR_TEST`), so no *t*-statistic can honestly be computed at all; its raw
  deltas flip sign at every horizon, exactly what a 5-point noise sample looks like. No
  certified reversal signal, in either reading.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The literature-closer pattern occurs about **once per 305
  ticker-years** — not a curiosity so much as a near-impossibility to trade — and even
  the far more frequent loose cut (once per ~4.2 ticker-years) fails certification and
  reverses sign at the longer horizons. Costs are not the binding constraint (most cells
  stay net-positive); the absence of statistical certification and of any usable event
  frequency both are.
- **"Beats a downtrend base rate?" — MIXED.** The loose cut points the right way at 1,
  5 and 10 days (small positive deltas, one nominally significant) before reversing at
  20 days; the strict cut's tiny sample flips sign at every horizon. Not backwards like
  a busted bearish-continuation pattern, and not confirmed like a real edge — genuinely
  mixed, and the strict cut's n = 5 is simply too thin to resolve further on this
  basket.
